questions.question: The sum of the length, the breadth and the height of a cuboid is 18 cm. If the length of its diagonal is 13 cm, then the total surface area of the cuboid is:
questions.solution:
Given:

The sum of the length, breadth and height of a cuboid is 18 cm. 

The length of its diagonal is 13 cm,

Formula used:

If the length, breadth, and height of a box are l, b, and h respectively

Then, the diagonal of the of the cuboid = √(l2 + b2 + h2)

The total surface area of the cuboid is = 2(lb + bh + bl)

**Calculation:**

As per the question,

Diagonal of the of the cuboid = 13

⇒ √(l2 + b2 + h2) = 13

⇒ (l2 + b2 + h2) = 169

Now,

(l + b + h) = 18

(l + b + h)² = 18²

⇒ (l2 + b2 + h2) + 2 (lb +bh+bl) = 324

⇒ 2 (lb +bh+bl) = 324 - 169

⇒ 155 cm²

**∴ The total surface area of the cuboid is 155 cm²**

questions.question: Ram bought an article for ₹6,800 and spent ₹700 on its repairs. He marked his article at 8% above the overall cost price. He sold the article for ₹6,196.50 after giving two successive discounts of 10% and x%,. Find the value of x.
questions.solution:

Ram bought an article for ₹6,800 and spent ₹700 on its repairs. 

He marked his article at 8% above the overall cost price. 

He sold the article for ₹6,196.50 after giving two successive discounts of 10% and x%

**Concept used:**

Total cost price = Article's cost price + spent on its repair

**Calculation:**

Total cost price = 6800 + 700

⇒ Rs 7500

So the market price = 7500 × (108 / 100)

⇒ Rs 8100

After 1st discount,

selling price = 8100 - 8100 × 10/100

⇒ 8100 - 810

⇒ Rs 7290

So 2nd discount amount = 7290 - 6,196.50

⇒ 1093.50

So 2nd discount percentage (x) = (1093.50 / 7290) × 100

⇒ 15%

**∴ The value of x is 15%**

questions.question: When the speed of a car is increased by 25%, it takes 24 minutes less to cover the same distance. What is the time (in hours) taken to cover the same distance at the actual speed?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

When the speed of a car is increased by 25%, it takes 24 minutes less to cover the same distance. 

**Formula:**

 Distance = Speed × Time

**Concept used:**

The speed ratio is inversely proportional to the time ratio.

**Calculation:**

Let, the speed of the car be 100 units

So after increased speed = (100 + 100 × 25/100) 

⇒ 100 + 25 = 125 units

So speed ratio is 100: 125 = 4: 5

So, the time ratio will be 5:4

Let, the time at 1st be 5x and then be 4x

As per the question 5x - 4x = 24 

⇒ x = 24 minutes 

So, initial time 

5x = 5 × 24

⇒ 120 minutes = 2hr

**∴ The time taken to cover the same distance at the actual speed is 2 hour**

questions.question: A and B can complete a work in 12 days and 18 days, respectively. They worked together for 4 days after which B was replaced by C and the remaining work was completed by A and C in the next 4 days. In how many days will C alone complete one-third of the same work?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

A and B can complete a work in 12 days and 18 days, respectively. 

They worked together for 4 days after which B was replaced by C 

And the remaining work was completed by A and C in the next 4 days.

**Concept used:**

Efficiency = (Total work / Total time taken)

Efficiency = work done in a single day 

**Calculation:**

Let total work be 36 units ( LCM of 12 and 18)

The efficiency of A = 36 /12 = 3 units

The efficiency of B = 36 / 18 = 2 units

So A + B together do in one day 3 + 2 = 5 units

So they do in 4 days 5 × 4 = 20 units

Remaining 36 - 20 = 16 units done by A + C in 4 days 

The efficiency of A + C = 4 units

So the efficiency of C = 4 - 3 = 1unit

So, C takes 36 / 1 = 36 days to do the total work

C, 36 / 3 = 12 days to do the one-third total work

**∴ C alone completed one-third of the same work in 12 days**

⇒ 4.4x

The selling price of the 2nd article is

5x + 5x × (20/100)

⇒ 5x + x

⇒ 6x

As per the question,

6x - 4.4x = 480

⇒ 1.6x = 480

⇒ x = 480 / 1.6

⇒ x = 300

So the total cost price of two article = 4x + 5x = 9x

Value of 9x = 9 × 300 = Rs 2700

**∴ The cost price is Rs 2700**

questions.question: Class X has 5 sections which have 40, 50, 50, 60 and 60 students, respectively. The pass per cent of these sections are 80%, 76%, 64%, 65% and 70%, respectively. The pass per cent of the entire class X (correct to two decimal places) is:
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Class X has 5 sections with 40, 50, 50, 60 and 60 students, respectively.

The pass per cent of these sections are 80%, 76%, 64%, 65% and 70%, respectively. 

**Calculation:**

Pass candidate Class X has 5 sections which have 40 students is 40 × 80 /100 = 32

Pass candidate Class X has 5 sections which have 50 students is 50 × 76 /100 = 38

Pass candidate Class X has 5 sections which have 50 students is 50 × 64 /100 = 32

Pass candidate Class X has 5 sections which have 60 students is 60 × 65 /100 = 39

Pass candidate Class X has 5 sections which have 60 students is 60 × 70 /100 = 42

Total number of candidates is 40 + 50 + 50 + 60 + 60 = 260

Total number of passing candidates is 32 + 38 + 32 + 39 + 42 = 183

Passing percentage (183 / 260) × 100 = 70.38 %

**The total Passing percentage is 70.38%**

questions.question: The average score of nineteen students in a computer examination is 74. It was detected that while working out the average by mistake the marks secured by one student was recorded as 65 in place of 56. What is the correct average score (correct to one decimal place)?
questions.solution:
Given: 

The average number of 19 students is 74

But by mistake, he writes the number 65 instead of 56

Concept Used:

Total number = Average × Number of students

Calculation:

The total number of 19 students is = (74 × 19) = 1406

By mistake, he wrote the number 65 instead of 56

So total increased value = 65 - 56 = 9

New, correct total number of 15 students = 1406 - 9 = 1397

So the correct average of these 15 numbers is = 1397 / 19 = 73.52

The actual average of these 19 students is 73.5
